programme.question: Define 'chaos' and 'debris' so they are provably distinct, prove or sharply state that chaos ends with a rate, and characterise what is left.

nodes.label: S1-S4 structure theorems
nodes.line: T1-T4 (layer histogram, octahedral confinement, firewall, kagome layers) and the twist lemma.

nodes.label: S5 threshold lemma
nodes.line: All chaos is driven by overcrowded cells; without them gump settles to period two.

nodes.label: S6 why three layers
nodes.line: In three or more layers no finite set of cells can die for good on its own.

nodes.label: S7 general confinement
nodes.line: Which lattices and rules confine patterns this way, and what hull shapes result.

nodes.label: S8 periodic patterns in the large
nodes.line: Densest still lifes, space-filling textures, growth of still-life counts.

nodes.label: D1 debris by dynamics
nodes.line: Debris = eventually free of overcrowding; misses the clockwork.

nodes.label: D2 debris by geometry
nodes.line: Debris: pockets too thin to hold chaos.

nodes.label: D1′ chaos by drive
nodes.line: Chaos = a positive rate of overcrowding events per cell.

nodes.label: D3 chaos by damage
nodes.line: Chaos = one flipped cell's damage spreads linearly (0.85 cube/gen).

nodes.label: D4 chaos by measure
nodes.line: Chaos = typical for a mixing invariant measure of density 0.4155.

nodes.label: M1 the face law
nodes.line: A face's wait grows exponentially with its area.

nodes.label: M2 conditional theorem
nodes.line: Good mixing of the steady state would imply exponential-in-area waits.

nodes.label: M3 noisy gump
nodes.line: With random deaths added, find matching upper and lower bounds.

nodes.label: M4 derive 0.208
nodes.line: Compute the per-cell cost from a model of the stationary state.

nodes.label: M5 symmetric collapse
nodes.line: Explain lockstep domains and the even/odd factor 1.5.

nodes.label: M6 single lineages memoryless?
nodes.line: Does one run's history carry memory between face deaths?

nodes.label: M7 firewall formation
nodes.line: Explain the ≈0.12 per cell cost of interior firewalls.

nodes.label: E1 ash census
nodes.line: What a typical seed leaves behind; no theory of its mix.

nodes.label: E2 random map with killing
nodes.line: A random-map model predicting how many states reach immortal cycles.
nodes.note: untested in PROGRAM; exponent F1 (unchecked) says it fails

nodes.label: E3 what the final collapse selects
nodes.line: Why side 15 goes extinct while side 16 leaves twelve S8b.

nodes.label: G1 a 2D gump
nodes.line: A flat cousin rule shows the same confinement, chaos and memoryless death.

nodes.label: G2 neighbours of gump
nodes.line: Which statements survive in nearby rules like B45/S3457 and B45/S3456.

nodes.label: G3 capped-threshold class
nodes.line: What singles out the rules that show the whole phenomenon.

theory_unchecked.warning: Nobody has checked theory/class.md or theory/exponent/ (STATUS.md 'In flight'). All items below are unchecked.

class_md.label: Gumps form a class
class_md.line: Rules of the 'capped threshold' type behave like gump when five listed conditions hold.

class_md.label: Many new gumps found
class_md.line: About ten other lattice-rule pairs, incl. FCC B45/S345 and BCC B34/S234, show the same behaviour.

class_md.label: Smallest gump has four neighbours
class_md.line: B2/S12 on the plain 2D four-neighbour grid works, though the agent's own criterion said it could not.

class_md.label: Not unique on its lattice
class_md.line: B456/S3456 shares gump's face law and lives at least 50× longer in octahedra.

class_md.label: Why the Moore neighbourhood fails
class_md.line: Only one cap is in reach of a face there, and that rule's bulk dies.

class_md.label: Forecast scorecard
class_md.line: Of 28 'gump' calls made in advance, 8 passed, 6 partial, 14 failed; the mean-field guide was at chance.

exponent.note: exponent.md is a stub (placeholder ⟦VERDICT⟧); results live in PREDICTIONS.md and theorems.md.

claims.label: Noisy toy: easy upper bound
claims.line: With random deaths at rate ε the mean wait is at most ε^(−L).

claims.label: Toy edge empties in three
claims.line: With the rows beneath chosen freely, any edge empties in three generations, never fewer in general.

claims.label: Right hypothesis is ratio mixing
claims.line: Decaying correlations are not enough for exponential waits; a ratio (ψ-) mixing bound is.

claims.label: Lemma A(c) is false
claims.line: The claim that any gump face can die in one generation is wrong (swarm critic's counterexample).

claims.label: Driven-face model reproduces gump
claims.line: Real top 4-5 layers on random noise match measured face lifetimes within 0.04 nats at A = 45, 63.

claims.label: 0.416 = 2×0.208 is not settled
claims.line: The toy's slope may sit at 0.36-0.41, so the factor two may be chance.

forecasts.label: Random map with killing fails
forecasts.outcome: headline hit; clauses (a) miss, (b) half, (c) hit, (d) miss

forecasts.label: Toy plunge lengthens with size
forecasts.outcome: miss (edge dies in a two-generation flash)

forecasts.label: 0.416 = 2×0.208 is chance
forecasts.outcome: (a) hit then softened by amendment; (b) miss; (c) hit

forecasts.label: Slope rises past A = 84
forecasts.outcome: no outcome recorded by the agent (not blind: written after seeing GPU numbers)

exponent.status: unchecked; agent stopped by usage limit before writing exponent.md

open_problems.label: Eventually periodic, bounded
open_problems.line: Every seed ends periodic within 2^N steps; the only rigorous bound.

open_problems.label: Dead faces stay dead
open_problems.line: A face layer that empties never refills, so the hull only shrinks.

open_problems.label: Exponential face law
open_problems.line: Wait for a face to die grows like exp(0.208 × area); measured, not proved.

open_problems.label: Chaos always ends?
open_problems.line: False as a theorem, plausibly true with overwhelming probability; random-map model untested.

open_problems.label: Characterising end states
open_problems.line: Only existence of a periodic end is proved; classification and the debris mix are open.

open_problems.label: Cubes outlive their ensembles?
open_problems.line: Side 16's long plateaus look like luck; fresh lineages show no memory.

open_problems.label: Even cubes tougher
open_problems.line: Vertex-centred cubes last ≈1.5× longer than odd ones at equal face area; no explanation.

open_problems.label: Symmetric-face slope
open_problems.line: Is the asymptotic slope exactly 0.209/6? GPU local slope 0.0329 ± 0.0011.

open_problems.label: Where cost per cell levels off
open_problems.line: Asymmetric faces cost 0.201 rising to 0.221 per cell up to A = 135.

open_problems.label: Interior firewall cost
open_problems.line: Firewalls cost ≈0.12 per band cell; no account.

open_problems.label: Favoured nine-cell state
open_problems.line: A dying symmetric face favours one nine-cell state 10×; not examined.

open_problems.label: Periods beyond 66
open_problems.line: Loops in 4- or 6-fold boxes could give periods 120-200.

open_problems.label: Signal-passing oscillators
open_problems.line: Can any oscillator pass a signal to another? None found.

open_problems.label: Clockwork not catalogued
open_problems.line: The 94 clockwork objects are not merged into the atlas.

open_problems.label: Neighbouring rules
open_problems.line: Does the face law hold, with another constant, in B45/S3457 and B45/S3456?

open_problems.label: Eppstein same as T2?
open_problems.line: Whether Eppstein's bounding-diamond argument is the same method; someone must read it.

open_problems.label: Novelty is absence of evidence
open_problems.line: No prior automaton on this lattice found; area law has prior art as supertransients.

open_problems.label: qsd.py over-counts
open_problems.line: The quasi-stationary tool is unreliable for symmetric soups below R = 30.

open_problems.label: No symmetry-reduced engine
open_problems.line: No single-state stepper fast enough for side 17; GPU ensembles exist.

refs.label: Eppstein: Life-like growth and decay
refs.line: Births cannot escape a bounding box or diamond in 2D Life-like rules; model for T2.

refs.label: Crutchfield–Kaneko
refs.line: Coupled map lattices whose chaotic transients grow faster than exponentially with size.

refs.label: Wackerbauer–Showalter
refs.line: Collapse of spatiotemporal chaos with exponential lifetimes in reaction–diffusion.

refs.label: Tél–Lai review
refs.line: The review of chaotic transients in extended systems.

refs.label: Politi–Torcini: stable chaos
refs.line: CA-like coupled maps with transients exponential in chain length.

refs.label: Houghton et al.
refs.line: Ginzburg–Landau chaos lasts exp(AL+B), then collapses at boundaries.
refs.authors: S. M. Houghton, E. Knobloch, S. M. Tobias, M. R. E. Proctor

refs.label: Durrett–Liu; Durrett–Schonmann
refs.line: Finite contact process in one dimension: extinction time exponential in size.
refs.authors: R. Durrett, X.-F. Liu; R. Durrett, R. H. Schonmann

refs.label: Mountford
refs.line: Finite multidimensional contact process: exponential limit law (1993); constant exists (1999).

refs.label: Bramson–Neuhauser
refs.line: Survival of 1D cellular automata under random perturbations: the one non-monotone theorem.

refs.label: Goles–Olivos
refs.line: Threshold networks have period ≤ 2: the basis of the threshold lemma.

refs.label: Darroch–Seneta
refs.line: Absorbing finite chains: quasi-stationary start gives exactly geometric death time.
